en.heading: 15 May: a new national day for King Sejong

en.heading: 14 July: a day recognizing people who have left North Korea
en.origin: North Korean Defectors Day is a South Korean national commemoration concerning the rights, inclusion and social participation of people who have left North Korea and settled in the South. The Ministry of the Interior documents a January 2024 instruction to create the day and Ministry of Unification consultations with defectors, associations and specialists in February. The government formally established 14 July in May 2024. This is an inclusion and public-awareness observance, not the anniversary of one border-crossing incident or a general public holiday. en.heading: Fourth Friday of April: remembering those who died on compulsory service

The government recognized the statutory memorial in November 2023, assigning the fourth Friday of April. It must be kept distinct from the broader Memorial Day on 6 June. en.heading: Third Saturday in October: Korea's changing Culture Day
en.origin: South Korea's Culture Day encourages public engagement with culture and the arts. Its modern framework followed the 1972 Culture and Arts Promotion Act and consolidated several older dates concerning broadcasting, cinema and magazines. On 30 March 1973 the government grouped these commemorations into Culture Day, initially observed on 20 October. A regulatory change on 6 September 2006 moved it to the third Saturday of October. The unified day preserves links to separate historical cultural institutions; it is not identical to the earliest broadcasting, film or magazine anniversary.
